- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early horizon (1–3 days); model often fails to reflect recent volatility; apply a 1–2% downward bias for 1–3 day horizon if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply a 2–4% downward adjustment if sentiment > 0.5 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of sentiment decay.
